## Descriptive statistics and visual evidence

\tightinputtable{../output/tables/tab_part2_descriptive_display.tex}

The four cells contain between
`r min(part2_summary$descriptive$N)` and
`r max(part2_summary$descriptive$N)` students. This imbalance motivates
effect-coded marginal tests rather than order-dependent sequential sums of
squares. Within-cell standard deviations range from
`r p2_fmt(min(part2_summary$descriptive$SD), 2)` to
`r p2_fmt(max(part2_summary$descriptive$SD), 2)` points. Completed preparation
and standard lunch are each descriptively associated with higher means, while
substantial score overlap remains in every cell.

\includefigure{../output/figures/fig_part2_histograms.pdf}{Within-cell mathematics-score histograms. Scores are bounded and discrete, with modest departures from Gaussian shape but no empty or extremely small cell.}{fig:part2-histograms}

\includefigure{../output/figures/fig_part2_factorial_patterns.pdf}{Boxplots and the mean interaction profile for lunch and test preparation. Near-parallel mean lines suggest a weak interaction relative to the two marginal differences.}{fig:part2-factorial-patterns}
